_comment: Harness capability manifest — OpenAI Codex. Everything projectstore ships for Codex is GENERATED from the source layout through this file; nothing under adapters/codex/ is hand-edited. To teach projectstore a third harness, copy this file, change the values, and run scripts/build-adapters.mjs — no surface file needs to change.

project_trust._comment: Codex loads a project's .codex/ layer — project config, project-local hooks — ONLY when the project is trusted, and silently skips all of it otherwise. User-level hooks are unaffected. Since projectstore installs hooks project-scoped by default, an untrusted project means the hooks never run and nothing says so: the exact silent failure the harness boundary exists to prevent. The installer checks this and refuses to claim success without it.

hook_review._comment: A SECOND gate, independent of project trust and the one that actually decides whether a hook runs. Codex requires each non-managed command hook to be reviewed and trusted individually, and records that trust against the hook's current HASH — so hooks appear in the settings list while being skipped, and any change to a hook definition (a reinstall that moves the checkout path, a version bump that rewrites the command) invalidates the approval and silently stops them again. This is deliberate security, not a defect: a project cannot make you run arbitrary commands by shipping a .codex/ directory. projectstore must never try to write into that trust store — the review is the user's to give.

tools._comment: Codex reports tool_name 'apply_patch' for every file edit, and ONE call can touch MANY files — the paths live in the patch envelope carried by tool_input.command, not in a file_path field. That is why path extraction is manifest-driven and returns a list. Codex emits PreToolUse/PostToolUse only for shell, unified_exec, apply_patch and mcp; reads are silent, which is fine — projectstore only ever scored writes.
tools._known_comment: Tools this harness reports that are NOT write paths. Purely to keep scripts/smoke-harness.mjs from flagging them when reading a recorded session — an unrecognised name there is worth a warning, a recognised read-only one is not. A shell is excluded on purpose: it can write, but it passes a command line rather than a path, so nothing is extractable and doctor's work-without-story check is the cover, exactly as on Claude Code.

hooks._comment: Codex's hook event names and its stdin/stdout JSON contract match Claude Code's for every event projectstore uses — same session_id/cwd/tool_name/tool_input on the way in, same hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext and top-level systemMessage on the way out. The event map is therefore an identity; it is written out in full anyway so a harness that renames an event only has to edit this table.

commands.scope_reason: Codex discovers custom prompts ONLY under $CODEX_HOME/prompts — there is no project-level prompts directory (openai/codex#4734, #9848 are open requests for one). A project-scoped install would silently ship no slash commands at all, so these stay user-level even when everything else is scoped to the project.

skills.scope_reason: Discovered from <project>/.codex/skills, and project skills take precedence over global ones of the same name.

hooks.scope_reason: Codex reads <repo>/.codex/hooks.json as well as the home copy. Scoping these is the whole point of a project install: user-level hooks fire in EVERY Codex project, costing a node process per tool call in repositories that have no vault bound.

agent_translation._comment: Codex custom agents are TOML, not Markdown+YAML: name/description/developer_instructions are required, and model/model_reasoning_effort/sandbox_mode are optional overrides that inherit from the parent session when omitted. `model` is deliberately NOT mapped — Codex model IDs are a different namespace and inventing a mapping would silently pin every agent to a model nobody chose; omitted means 'inherit the session', which is the honest default. Effort maps because the scale is comparable: model_reasoning_effort accepts minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh, so projectstore max becomes xhigh. Mapping it to high would cap the agents two notches below what bind.md promises the user, silently. The `tools:` allowlist has no Codex analogue, so it is translated into the one thing it was actually being used to express: every bundled agent is read-only.
agent_translation.model_preset_advice: Do not offer a preset list: model IDs are harness-specific and any list hardcoded here goes stale. Ask the user to name a model their own Codex install offers (`/model` lists them), or to skip — skipping leaves the key unset, and an agent with no model inherits the session's, which is the sane default.
agent_translation._model_presets_comment: The bundled agents ship `model: opus` in frontmatter, which is why model_map is empty: opus does not exist on Codex, and translating it would pin every agent to a model nobody chose. That was already handled. What was NOT: the /projectstore-agents and /projectstore-bind prompts offered opus/fable/sonnet as a CHOICE, so a Codex user could pick a model that does not exist there and have it written into projectstore.json and passed as a spawn parameter.

capabilities._comment: No statusline slot exists in Codex, so that surface is dropped rather than faked. The approval gate is prose here because Codex has no AskUserQuestion tool — NOT because it lacks a structural mechanism: PreToolUse can return permissionDecision:deny on both harnesses, and projectstore uses it on neither yet. Do not describe that as a Codex advantage.

lint._comment: Regexes that mark a fragment as harness-specific. This list carries only what CANNOT be derived from the manifests — product names, command namespaces, UI affordances. Another harness write-tool names and environment variables are generated by lintPatterns() in scripts/harness.mjs, because a hand-written list only ever contains what someone already thought of. A match in a generated file must be covered by a `from` rule in EVERY emitting harness, or tests/portability.test.mjs fails and names the file, the token and the manifests missing a rule. This is the half of the mechanism that makes a NEW feature portable by default: you cannot land a command that only Claude Code can run.
lint._allow_comment: Literal phrases exempt from the DERIVED tool-name patterns, each one a place where a write-tool name is not a tool reference: an approval-option label the user picks between, or an ordinary English verb at the start of a sentence. All of them read identically on every harness. Keep this list short and justified — it is a hole in the guard, and the preferred remedy is always to rephrase the source so it names no tool at all (which is what removed roughly twenty other entries).

update_instructions: **Keeping projectstore current**: this harness installs from a checkout, not a marketplace.
Pull the checkout and re-run `node scripts/install-harness.mjs`, then restart Codex.
